dupset.definition: Two rows are duplicates when their prompts meet any one of three tests: (1) containment (A0.5): word 5-gram containment |A & B| / min(|A|, |B|) >= 0.5 over re.findall(r'\w+', prompt.lower()) (a prompt of fewer than five tokens is one gram of all its tokens); (2) opening (W15): the first 15 of those tokens are identical (a prompt of fewer than 15 tokens never matches); (3) pattern (C): both rows are WeirdChat with the same meta.pattern_id. Union-find over the edges of all three tests; the first row of each group in row order is kept, the others are duplicates. A replacement must meet none of the three tests with any of the parent's rows (kept or removed) or any earlier pick.

selection.rule: Slots in parent row order. A WildChat slot takes the best remaining WildChat candidate; a WeirdChat slot the best remaining candidate of the removed row's behavior_id, and when that behaviour has none left, the best remaining candidate of the behaviour with the fewest WeirdChat rows in the population built so far (ties by SHA256(ASCII("16:" + behavior_id)); behaviours with none left skipped). Best = tier 1 before tier 2, then the smallest SHA256(ASCII("16:" + scenario_id)), ties by scenario_id; candidates a screen failed are skipped for the reason recorded, and so is a candidate that is a duplicate by the definition (word 5-gram containment >= 0.5, the same first 15 lower-cased word tokens, or the same WeirdChat pattern_id) of any of the 500 rows of the previous population, kept or removed, or of an earlier pick of this derivation (each such skip recorded where the rule reached it)
